title_en: Amendments to Payment Services Act Regarding Stablecoin Issuance and Intermediation
title_ja: 資金決済法改正案（ステーブルコインの発行・仲介に関する事項）
summary_en: The Financial Services Agency (FSA) is seeking public comments on draft amendments to the Payment Services Act expanding the categories of entities permitted to issue and intermediate fiat-backed stablecoins, clarifying segregated asset rules for issuers, and adjusting reporting obligations for intermediary businesses.
business_impact_en: Foreign crypto-asset service providers, payment institutions, and stablecoin issuers offering services to Japanese users may face new licensing categories, capital and segregation requirements, and expanded AML/CFT and travel-rule obligations.
recommended_action_en: Inventory current and planned stablecoin-related products; map them against the proposed licensing categories; assess capital, governance, and AML implications; and consider submitting comments before the deadline if material concerns or ambiguities exist.

title_en: Proposed Amendments to the Act on the Protection of Personal Information (APPI)
title_ja: 個人情報保護法改正案
summary_en: The Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC) has submitted draft amendments to the Diet introducing stricter rules on cross-border data transfers, expanded data subject rights (including a clearer right to deletion in specified circumstances), and increased administrative fines for serious violations involving large-scale data leakage or willful misuse.
business_impact_en: Foreign companies processing personal data of Japanese residents, including via overseas affiliates or vendors, must reassess cross-border transfer mechanisms, vendor agreements, privacy notices, breach response procedures, and records of processing.
recommended_action_en: Update transfer impact assessments, refresh privacy notices in Japanese and English, review and amend data processing agreements with overseas affiliates and vendors, and brief incident-response teams on the revised notification thresholds.

title_en: Mandatory Climate-Related Disclosures in Annual Securities Reports for Large Listed Companies
title_ja: 大規模上場会社における有価証券報告書での気候関連情報開示の義務化
summary_en: The Cabinet has approved an order amending the Cabinet Office Ordinance on Disclosure of Corporate Affairs, requiring large listed companies to disclose climate-related governance, strategy, risk management, and Scope 1, 2, and selected Scope 3 emissions data in their annual securities reports (yuka shoken hokokusho), aligned with the SSBJ framework.
business_impact_en: Japanese subsidiaries of foreign-listed parents, and foreign issuers listed in Japan, may need to align local disclosure timelines and methodologies with parent-level sustainability reporting (ISSB / CSRD), and prepare consolidated emissions data on a Japanese-fiscal-year basis.
recommended_action_en: Confirm the scope of consolidated disclosure, prepare GHG emissions data collection workflows with finance and operations teams, and coordinate timing and assurance scope with parent company ESG and audit teams.

title_en: Revised Cybersecurity Management Guidelines for Critical Infrastructure Operators
title_ja: 重要インフラ事業者向けサイバーセキュリティ対策指針 改訂案
summary_en: The Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) and the National center of Incident readiness and Strategy for Cybersecurity (NISC) have published revised draft guidelines covering supply-chain risk management, incident reporting timelines, third-party software inventory (SBOM) expectations, and board-level cybersecurity governance.
business_impact_en: Operators in energy, telecommunications, finance, transportation, healthcare, and other critical sectors, including foreign-owned Japanese subsidiaries, should expect tightened audit expectations, supply-chain due diligence requirements, and clearer board accountability for cyber incidents.
recommended_action_en: Benchmark current cybersecurity governance and incident-response playbooks against the revised draft, prepare a gap analysis, engage vendors on SBOM availability, and consider submitting public comments where guidance is ambiguous.
source_name: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)

title_en: Enforcement Guidelines under the Freelance Protection Act
title_ja: フリーランス・事業者間取引適正化等法 運用ガイドライン
summary_en: The Japan Fair Trade Commission (JFTC) and the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) have jointly issued enforcement guidelines under the Act on Securing Proper Transactions Involving Specified Entrusted Business Operators ('Freelance Protection Act'), clarifying mandatory written terms, the 60-day payment deadline rule, prohibited conduct such as unilateral fee reductions, and harassment-prevention obligations.
business_impact_en: Companies engaging individual contractors in Japan, including foreign companies engaging Japan-based freelancers, must review their written engagement terms, ensure payment within 60 days of delivery, and confirm internal controls against prohibited acts and harassment.
recommended_action_en: Audit existing freelancer contracts and onboarding workflows; update standard templates to reflect the disclosure, payment-term, and harassment-prevention requirements; and train procurement and HR staff on the new enforcement posture.
